title: Astronauts Grow Taller in Space 🚀 #shorts
description:
In microgravity the spine is no longer squeezed by gravity, so astronauts can grow up to 3% taller – about 2 inches for a 6-foot person. NASA astronaut Scott Kelly came back from 340 days on the International Space Station about 2 inches taller, and was back to his normal height within about two days. The downside: studies link long spaceflights to weaker back muscles, and astronauts have about four times the risk of a herniated disc.

Sources: Space.com / Scientific American, CNN, Fox News, Smithsonian Magazine, UC San Diego study in Spine (2016), Wikipedia (Intervertebral disc damage and spaceflight)

#shorts #facts #crazyfacts #space #humanbody #didyouknow
comment: Would you go to space for a year to be 2 inches taller for two days? 🚀👇

scenes.headline:
ASTRONAUTS
GROW TALLER
IN SPACE

scenes.text: On Earth, gravity squeezes your spine all day long. In space, that pressure is gone.
So the spine stretches out, and astronauts can grow up to three percent taller.
scenes.label: TALLER IN SPACE

scenes.text: For a six-foot person, that's about two extra inches.
NASA astronaut Scott Kelly spent three hundred forty days on the space station, and came home about two inches taller.
scenes.label: DAYS IN SPACE

scenes.text: But gravity won fast. In about two days, he was back to his normal height.
And there's a catch. Astronauts are about four times more likely to get a slipped disc.
So space makes you taller... but your back pays the price.
